canonical_name: Minimum-cost flow and circulation theorem family (exact proposition open)
source_attribution: Many mathematicians, twentieth century (catalog metadata only; no citation)
statement_blocker: The repository supplies a problem-family label and the gloss 'costed network flow', not an ordered-binder proposition. It does not choose minimum-cost circulation, fixed-value minimum-cost flow, minimum-cost maximum flow, transshipment, existence or attainment, integrality, LP duality, negative-residual-cycle or price optimality, or correctness and complexity of any algorithm. It also omits the graph and edge model, terminals or node balances, capacity and lower bounds, numeric carriers, feasibility and boundedness hypotheses, objective, conclusion, and boundary cases. Selecting one candidate without accountable source approval would invent proposition-changing scope.
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted source must fix finite directed graph or multigraph data; vertex and edge carriers; source/sink, prescribed value, node balances, or circulation scope; capacity, lower-bound, flow, and cost carriers; feasibility and objective sets; universes; and every finiteness, decidability, order, algebraic, and asymptotic context.
conclusion: Open: the catalog does not select an existence or attainment result, residual-cycle or price optimality characterization, integral optimum, primal-dual equality, algorithm correctness or termination, running-time theorem, or a conjunction of separately modeled claims.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no proposition is selected; statement work must resolve every network, balance, capacity, cost, feasibility, optimum, algorithm, and boundary case listed in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: existence or attainment of a minimum-cost feasible circulation or flow
minimum cost among flows of one prescribed source-to-sink value
minimum-cost circulation iff absence of a negative residual cycle, as in Goldberg-Tarjan Theorem 2.1
minimum-cost circulation iff existence of a price potential with nonnegative residual reduced costs, as in Theorem 3.1
integrality or primal-dual equality under source-selected integer and feasibility assumptions
correctness, termination, iteration count, or running time of cycle canceling, cancel-and-tighten, cost scaling, successive shortest paths, network simplex, or another algorithm
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty, singleton, two-vertex, no-edge, disconnected, and source-equals-sink networks
terminals absent from the vertex carrier and balances whose total is nonzero
zero required flow, infeasible capacity or lower-bound constraints, and empty feasible sets
zero, negative, or infinite capacities and lower bounds
zero and negative arc costs, negative residual cycles, zero-cost cycles, and unbounded objectives
self-loops, parallel and antiparallel arcs, and edge-indexed versus vertex-pair encodings
multiple optimal flows or prices and nonattained infimum formulations
natural, integer, rational, nonnegative-real, real, and extended-value data
invalid starting states, nondeterministic algorithm choices, nontermination, and small-input asymptotics
unit-cost versus bit-cost arithmetic, data-structure operations, and exact versus executable computation
excluded_substitutions: max-flow/min-cut equality or a maximum-flow algorithm without the selected cost objective
generic network flow, multicommodity flow, shortest path, assignment, matching, or transportation statements without a checked source-mapped reduction
minimum-cost circulation silently substituted for prescribed-value flow or minimum-cost maximum flow, or conversely
negative-cycle or price optimality advertised as existence, integrality, algorithm termination, or complexity
one named minimum-cost-flow algorithm substituted for an unidentified theorem family
a structure, hypothesis, optimizer, price, residual cycle, starting execution, or cost certificate that stores the requested conclusion
a finite solver run, benchmark, floating-point output, URL, title match, or the untrusted catalog label used as proof credit
